learning_objective: 🎯 Let us become grammar detectives and find out who the sentence is about (Subject) and what they are doing (Predicate)!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Every sentence has a star! The Subject is the person, place, or thing the sentence is talking about. Example: 'The cute dog' barks loudly.
The Predicate tells us what the star (Subject) is doing or feeling. It always contains the verb! Example: The cute dog 'barks loudly'.
In command sentences like 'Close the door!', where is the subject? It is a secret! The subject is always 'You', even if it is hidden and not written.

fun_activity.title: ✂️ The Sentence Chop
fun_activity.instructions: Write 'My best friend loves eating pizza.' on a piece of paper. Draw a line right down the middle to chop the Subject away from the Predicate!

quick_recap: ⭐ The Subject tells us WHO or WHAT the sentence is about.
⭐ The Predicate tells us what the Subject DOES or IS.
⭐ In imperative (command) sentences, the Subject is always a hidden 'You'.
